raw_response:
I am old now, so I do not toss money around. On these 5 mu, I will still do wheat and maize the same way as most people here, because this rotation is steady and I know it well. Last year this way still gave me grain and did not leave the land idle. I only have two people in the house, so I keep things simple, use the well when the crop really needs water, and follow the local timing. I watch my neighbors too. If the wheat stays green and the spring rain is decent, I will not push too much extra fertilizer. But I also do not dare cut too much, because if wheat turns yellow or maize is weak, losing yield hurts more than saving a few yuan.

For wheat, I would keep a normal local improved variety, sow in early October, put most fertilizer before sowing and a second round around jointing. I would irrigate around overwintering, jointing, and grain filling if the weather is dry, because our well water costs money, but wheat here usually needs a few waters to be safe. After wheat harvest in June, I will hurry and plant maize right away. That gap is very short, so I will use light rotary tillage or direct sow after the straw is handled. For maize, I will use hybrid seed, put some fertilizer at sowing and some later before the big growth stage, and irrigate once if summer rain is not enough. I am not chasing the highest yield, just a steady harvest with spending I can manage.
